A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of stop-gradient (SG) and exponential-moving-average (EMA) learning. The complete text, equations, figures, table, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-classification experiments in Appendix A and numerical simulations in Appendix B, including Figures 2–4 and Table 1.

after.justification: V2 retains original video-classification results in Section 2.3 and numerical simulation results in Section 3.3, including Figures 2–4.

M1.justification: The SG and EMA updates, encoder/predictor framework, and loss formulations are retained. V2 adds mathematical characterizations without changing the learning procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use Kinetics710 and SSv2 for representation learning, K400 and SSv2 for classification evaluation, and scalar-input synthetic simulations with two-dimensional embeddings. V2's n = 2 wording corrects v1's inconsistent m = 2 description of the same simulations.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison remains SG versus EMA. Both versions also quote the same V-JEPA ViT-L reference accuracies, 72.9 and 67.4. The additional related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported video settings and illustrative trajectory settings match. However, v1 specifies 4,000 integration steps, a convergence tolerance of 10^-5 R, and reporting restricted to cases with discriminant at least zero for the 10,000-trial study. V2 omits these specifications while changing the convergence finding, leaving uncertain whether the corresponding evaluation conditions remained identical.

E4.justification: Both retain the same loss, parameter-increment, downstream-accuracy, trajectory, and convergence analyses. No new empirical ablation, robustness test, or sensitivity analysis appears. The added equilibrium-stability analysis is theoretical.

E5.justification: Both report 10,000 randomized simulation trials and the same parameter and initialization distributions. Neither supplies confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty for the video experiments. The revised convergence finding does not establish a change in statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 reports 99.9% EMA convergence and 100.0% SG convergence; v2 Section 3.3 says both algorithms always converge. V2 repeats the outer-circle percentages, 92.8% for EMA and 82.0% for SG, and retains the plotted results in Figures 2–4. The changed convergence statement is not an established same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition 3.5 and Corollary 3.6, characterizing full-rank linear equilibria through quadratic equations for S = A^T A and associated algebraic varieties. Proposition 3.10 extends v1's scalar radius calculation with a saddle-versus-stable classification and proof. The general stability proof is substantially revised, while v1's derivation of conditions for equilibria also to be critical points of the original objective, Equations (31)–(32), is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add explicit characterization of linear equilibria as a central contribution. V2 also presents the retained real-data and simulation findings as main empirical contributions, whereas v1 describes them as preliminary appendix investigations. The central non-optimization and collapse-avoidance claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 newly explains the absence of inner-circle convergence through saddle points and treats scalar inputs as an exceptional case, asserting that such saddles do not occur for m > 1. It also strengthens the explanation of generic validity to 'always in practice' and removes v1's explicit warning about limited simulation sampling. These changes materially alter the interpretation and applicability of the stability claims.

D1.justification: Removing Table 1 also removes the simulation convergence tolerance, integration budget, and restriction on which trials enter the reported statistics. V2 adds a reproducibility statement explicitly describing the underlying V-JEPA code as publicly available. Most video implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially expands the research positioning around feature-decorrelation and asymmetry-based methods. Added discussions include whitening losses, random-class collapse prevention, unified gradient analyses, implicit decorrelation, and explicit predictors. V2 also more specifically contrasts its assumptions and equilibrium characterization with Tian et al. and Littwin et al.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and contribution narrative. The empirical appendices become Sections 2.3 and 3.3, while proofs are collected in the final appendix, Section 5. It also adds ethics and reproducibility statements and changes the author block.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different title, author, heading, and running-header layout. Figures 2–4 move into the main text; Figure 2 changes from three rows by two columns to two rows by three columns, with revised captions and an added EMA distance-axis label. Table 1 disappears, with most of its findings summarized in prose.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a useful equilibrium characterization and broader research context, but its continuous equilibrium families in Corollary 3.6 remain unreconciled with the pointwise asymptotic-stability claim in Definition 3.7 and Proposition 3.9. Empirical reporting also weakens: v1's 99.9% EMA convergence becomes 'always' while convergence and filtering details disappear. These substantive theoretical and reporting tradeoffs prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
